chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the prayer in Medina (Qum), is it like the prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? He said: 'No, indeed, the prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is equivalent to one thousand prayers, and the prayer in Medina is like the prayer in other cities.'

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةُ: The city (specifically Qum in this context)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Mosque of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between praying in the Prophet's mosque and other cities according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific distinction between the Prophet's Mosque in Medina and the general city of Medina, noting that the thousand-fold reward is exclusive to the former, while the latter holds the same merit as other cities. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the unique sanctity of Masjid al-Nabi compared to other significant locations like Qum or Mecca. The hadith underscores the principle that while all mosques are blessed, certain sites possess a divinely ordained superiority in spiritual reward.
